result.topic_en: A page of Gauss's mathematical diary for August–September 1796 (Göttingen) recording results on congruences, the golden theorem (quadratic reciprocity), roots of unity, power sums of roots of equations, an infinite series, the factorisation of x^π−1 modulo p, and the asymptotic density 6/π² of reduced fractions.
result.transcription:
*$a^{2^n+1}(p) \equiv 1$ semper solvere in potestate  Aug. 3 Gött. ${}^2$
Rationem theorematis aurei quomodo [-altius-] profun-
dius perscrutari oporteat perspexi et ad hoc accingor
supra [-primam-] quadraticas aequationes egredi cona-
tus. Inventio formularum quae semper per primos:
$\sqrt[n]{1}$ (numerice) dividi possunt  Aug. 13 Ibid.
Obiter $(a+b\sqrt{-1})^{m+n\sqrt{-1}}$ evolutum  — 14
Rei summa iamiam intellecta. restat ut singu-  — 16. G.
la muniantur
$(a^p) \equiv (a)$ mod. p., a radix aequationis cuiuscunque
quomodocunque irrationalis.  18
Si P, Q functiones alg. quantitatis indeterminatae fuerint inc. ${}^2$
Datur $tP+uQ=1$ [-tum-] in algebra tum specio- 19 G.
sa tum numerica.
Exprimuntur potestates radicum aequationis propositae
aggregatae per coefficientes aequationis lege perquam
simplici. (cum aliis quibusdam geometr. in Exerc.)  21. G.
Summatio seriei infinitae $1+\frac{x^n}{1\ldots n}+\frac{x^{2n}}{1\ldots 2n}$ &c  eod.
*Minutiis quibusdam exceptis feliciter scopum
attigi scil. si $p^n \equiv 1 \pmod{\pi}$ fore $x^{\pi}-1$ compositum
e factoribus graduum n non excedentibus [-cuidi-][?] & proin
aequationem conditionalem fore solubilem.  Sept. 2 G.
unde duas theor: aurei dem. nov[?] deduxi.
Numerus fractionum inaequalium quarum denominatores certum limitem
non superat ad numerum fractionum omnium quarum num. aut
denom. sint diversi infra eundem limitem in infinito ut $6:\pi\pi$  Sept. 6.

methods.what: Solving the congruence a^(2^n+1) ≡ 1 mod p in powers
Formulas for primes dividing expressions built from n-th roots of unity
methods.quote:
Inventio formularum quae semper per primos:
$\sqrt[n]{1}$ (numerice) dividi possunt

methods.what: Expansion of a complex number raised to a complex power
Fermat-type congruence for algebraic roots: a^p ≡ a mod p for a root of any equation
methods.quote:
$(a^p) \equiv (a)$ mod. p., a radix aequationis cuiuscunque
quomodocunque irrationalis.

methods.what: Bezout identity for coprime polynomials, symbolic and numerical
methods.quote:
Datur $tP+uQ=1$ [-tum-] in algebra tum specio- 19 G.
sa tum numerica.

methods.what: Power sums of the roots of an equation expressed through its coefficients (Newton-type identities)
methods.quote:
Exprimuntur potestates radicum aequationis propositae
aggregatae per coefficientes aequationis lege perquam
simplici.

methods.what: Summation of the series 1 + x^n/n! + x^{2n}/(2n)! + ...
If p^n ≡ 1 mod π then x^π − 1 factors mod p into factors of degree at most n, making the conditional equation solvable
methods.quote:
si $p^n \equiv 1 \pmod{\pi}$ fore $x^{\pi}-1$ compositum
e factoribus graduum n non excedentibus [-cuidi-][?] & proin
aequationem conditionalem fore solubilem.

methods.what: Two new proofs of quadratic reciprocity derived from this
methods.quote: unde duas theor: aurei dem. nov[?] deduxi.

methods.what: Asymptotic proportion of reduced fractions with bounded denominators is 6/π²

items.quote:
Rationem theorematis aurei quomodo [-altius-] profun-
dius perscrutari oporteat perspexi et ad hoc accingor
supra [-primam-] quadraticas aequationes egredi cona-
tus.
items.english: I have seen how the reason of the golden theorem must be examined more deeply, and I am setting about this, attempting to go beyond quadratic equations.

items.quote:
Rei summa iamiam intellecta. restat ut singu-  — 16. G.
la muniantur
items.english: The main point of the matter is now understood; it remains for the details to be secured.

items.quote:
Minutiis quibusdam exceptis feliciter scopum
attigi
items.english: Apart from certain minor details, I have happily reached the goal.

items.quote:
Numerus fractionum inaequalium quarum denominatores certum limitem
non superat ad numerum fractionum omnium quarum num. aut
denom. sint diversi infra eundem limitem in infinito ut $6:\pi\pi$
items.english: The number of unequal fractions whose denominators do not exceed a certain limit is to the number of all fractions whose numerators or denominators are different below the same limit, in the limit, as 6 : π².
